definition_zh: 补偿；赔偿金；报酬；弥补
definition_en: money paid to someone for loss or injury, or something that balances a disadvantage
core_image: 天平一端缺了砝码，另一端补上同等重量
scene: 工地摔伤之后，公司按合同支付了一笔款项。The worker received compensation for his injury.
sceneCN: 这里 compensation 指「赔偿金」（第 1 个义项：为损失支付的补偿）；句意是这名工人因受伤得到了赔偿。

senses.title: Payment for loss
senses.definition: money paid to someone because they have suffered loss or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因遭受损失或伤害而支付给某人的钱
senses.example: The family received compensation for the damaged house.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人因房屋受损获得了赔偿。
senses.why: When loss cannot be undone, money is offered to make the balance level again.
senses.whyCN: 损失无法挽回时，用钱把天平重新找平。

senses.title: Pay for work
senses.definition: the money and benefits paid for a job
senses.definitionCN: 为一份工作支付的金钱与福利
senses.example: The job offers good compensation and free meals.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作报酬不错，还管饭。
senses.why: Work is also a cost to the worker, so pay is framed as making it even.
senses.whyCN: 工作对劳动者也是付出，因此工资被说成把账找平。

senses.title: Something that balances a flaw
senses.definition: something good that balances a disadvantage
senses.definitionCN: 用来抵消缺点的好处
senses.example: The quiet garden is compensation for the small rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的花园弥补了房间狭小。
senses.why: Not all debts are paid in money; a good point can answer a bad one.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有亏欠都用钱偿还，一个优点也能抵消一个缺点。

intro.en: Compensation comes from Latin compensare, to weigh one thing against another until they balance.
intro.cn: compensation 来自拉丁语 compensare，意为把一物与另一物相称，直到两边平衡。

items.en: Pensare meant to weigh or to pay out.
items.cn: pensare 意为称重或称量支付。

items.en: Compensare meant to balance one sum against another.
items.cn: compensare 意为用一笔抵另一笔，使两边相平。

items.en: Compensatio named the settling of that balance.
items.cn: compensatio 指把这笔账找平。

items.en: Old French compensation kept the bookkeeping sense.
items.cn: 古法语 compensation 保留了记账式的含义。

items.en: English compensation widened to injury, pay and any offset.
items.cn: 英语 compensation 扩展到伤害赔偿、薪酬与任何抵消。

note.en: The look-alike group holds related but different -tion nouns, and the meaning group separates repayment, damages and salary.
note.cn: 形近组收的是相关却不同的名词，近义组分辨偿还款项、损害赔偿金与薪水。

entries.definition: to pay someone for a loss
the way parts are put together
money a court orders for harm done

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a short weight on one pan, then move to pay for work and to a good point that answers a bad one.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一端缺了砝码开始，再走到工作的报酬以及用一个优点抵消一个缺点。

normal.en: Com- is together and pens means weigh, so compensation is the weight added to level the pans.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pens 是称重，compensation 就是补上去把那两盘称平的重量。

normal.en: Compensate is the verb and compensation the noun of the same settling.
normal.cn: compensate 是动词，compensation 是同一次找平的名词。

normal.en: You claim compensation, and a firm pays it.
normal.cn: 你提出索赔，公司支付赔偿。

normal.en: A compensation package is pay plus holidays plus insurance.
normal.cn: 薪酬方案是工资加假期再加保险。

normal.en: The view from the top floor is compensation for the stairs.
normal.cn: 顶楼的风景，是对爬楼梯的弥补。

abstract.en: Picture one pan of a balance rising, then a hand adding weight.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一端翘起，一只手往上加砝码。

abstract.en: Picture a pay slip folded inside a white envelope.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工资条折好放在白信封里。

abstract.en: Picture a small balcony that makes a tiny flat worth living in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小阳台，让一间小公寓值得住下去。

examples.en: She asked for compensation after the delay.
examples.cn: 延误之后她要求赔偿。

examples.en: The company paid compensation to the farmers.
examples.cn: 公司向农民支付了赔偿。

examples.en: Working from home is some compensation for the long hours.
examples.cn: 在家办公算是对长时间工作的一种弥补。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compensation 记成 com（一起）加 pens（称重）加 ation：把两边的重量称平，就是补偿。

root: 源自拉丁语 compensare，com- 表示一起，pensare 表示称重，本义是把两边称平，后引申为赔偿金、报酬与弥补。

sensesIntro.en: From money that levels a loss, to pay for work, and finally to any good point that answers a bad one.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把损失称平的赔偿，到工作的报酬，最后到任何抵消缺点的好处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pan of a balance is short of weight, so a matching weight is added.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一端缺了砝码，另一端补上同等重量。

branches.en: Money for injury is the clearest modern sense.
branches.cn: 为伤害付钱是现代最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Pay treats work as a cost that must be made even.
branches.cn: 工资把劳动看作一份需要找平的付出。

branches.en: Not every debt is money, yet every debt wants balance.
branches.cn: 并非每笔亏欠都是钱，但每笔亏欠都想要平衡。

branches.en: Both are settled on the same old balance.
branches.cn: 两者都在同一台古老的天平上了结。

branches.en: A good point and a sum of money both answer a loss.
branches.cn: 一个优点与一笔钱，都在回应一份损失。

intro.en: Compensation joins the verb compensate with the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: compensation 由动词 compensate 加名词后缀 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pensare, to weigh, also gives us pensive and pension.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pensare（称重）还给出了 pensive 与 pension 这样的词。

items.example: The small compensations made the job bearable.
items.exampleCN: 那些小小的补偿让这份工作还过得去。

items.meaning: to make up for a loss
items.example: Nothing can compensate for the lost time.
items.exampleCN: 什么也弥补不了失去的时间。

items.example: Good coffee compensates for a poor view.
items.exampleCN: 好咖啡弥补了视野不佳。
工人们得到了全额补偿。

items.example: He worked late as a compensating effort.

items.exampleCN: 法院判给了补偿性款项。

items.meaning: a person or device that compensates
items.example: The device acts as a heat compensator.
items.exampleCN: 这个装置起热补偿作用。

items.example: The loss is compensable under the law.
items.exampleCN: 这种损失依法可获补偿。

definition_zh: 竞争；比赛；争夺
definition_en: to try to be more successful than others, or to take part in a contest
core_image: 两名跑者在同一条跑道上并排冲向终点
scene: 小店老板把价格压到最低，仍担心对面新开的店。Small shops find it hard to compete with big chains.
sceneCN: 这里 compete 指「竞争」（第 1 个义项：争取胜过他人）；句意是小店很难与大型连锁店竞争。

senses.title: To strive against others
senses.definition: to try hard to gain something that others also want
senses.definitionCN: 努力争取别人也想要的东西
senses.example: Five firms competed for the same contract.
senses.exampleCN: 五家公司争夺同一份合同。
senses.why: Two parties reaching for one prize is the oldest shape of the word.
senses.whyCN: 两方伸手去够同一个奖赏，是这个词最古老的样子。

senses.title: To take part in a contest
senses.definition: to take part in a race, match or game
senses.definitionCN: 参加赛跑、比赛或竞技
senses.example: She competed in three events at the games.
senses.exampleCN: 她在运动会上参加了三个项目。
senses.why: From striving, the word narrows to a formal contest with rules and a finish.
senses.whyCN: 从努力争取，这个词收窄到有规则与终点的正式比赛。

intro.en: Compete comes from Latin competere, to seek something together, from com, together, and petere, to seek.
intro.cn: compete 来自拉丁语 competere，意为一起追求某物，由 com（一起）与 petere（追求）构成。

items.en: Petere meant to seek, to aim at or to ask for.
items.cn: petere 意为寻求、瞄准或请求。

items.en: Competere meant to seek the same thing as another.
items.cn: competere 意为与别人追求同一样东西。

items.en: It also meant to be fit for a task or an office.
items.cn: 它也指适合某项任务或职位。

items.en: Old French competir narrowed it to rivalry.
items.cn: 古法语 competir 把词义收窄到争胜。

items.en: English compete covered both trade rivals and sports.
items.cn: 英语 compete 同时覆盖商业对手与体育竞技。

note.en: The look-alike group holds verbs one letter away from compete, and the meaning group ranks the verbs of rivalry.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compete 只差一个字母的动词，近义组排出表示争胜的动词。

entries.definition: to obey a rule or request
to be as good as another

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one prize and many hands, then move to shops that cut prices and to races with rules.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个奖赏与许多只手开始，再走到压价的小店与有规则的赛跑。

normal.en: Com- is together and pete means seek, so compete is to seek the same thing together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pete 是寻求，compete 就是一起去求同一样东西。

normal.en: Compete with a rival, compete for a prize, compete in a race.
normal.cn: 与对手 compete with，为奖品 compete for，在赛场上 compete in。

normal.en: The noun is competition, the person is a competitor.
normal.cn: 名词是 competition，人就是 competitor。

normal.en: Competitive prices keep a small shop alive.
normal.cn: 有竞争力的价格让小店的活路得以延续。

normal.en: You cannot compete if you never enter.
normal.cn: 不进场，就谈不上竞争。

abstract.en: Picture two hands reaching for one last ticket.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手同时伸向最后一张票。

abstract.en: Picture two shops posting new prices in one morning.
abstract.cn: 想象两家店在同一个早上挂出新价签。

abstract.en: Picture five swimmers bent on the blocks, waiting for the whistle.
abstract.cn: 想象五名泳者伏在出发台上，等着哨声。

examples.en: Small firms must compete on quality.
examples.cn: 小公司必须在质量上竞争。

examples.en: He competed against runners from ten countries.
examples.cn: 他与来自十个国家的跑者同场竞技。

examples.en: Two cities competed for the new factory.
examples.cn: 两座城市争夺这家新工厂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compete 记成 com（一起）加 pete（寻求）：大家一起伸手去求同一个东西，就是竞争。

root: 源自拉丁语 competere，com- 表示一起，petere 表示追求，本义是一起追求同一个目标，后引申为竞争与参赛。

sensesIntro.en: From striving for one prize, to entering a contest with rules.
sensesIntro.cn: 从为同一个奖赏而努力，到参加有规则的比赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two runners side by side on one track, driving toward the same line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两名跑者在同一条跑道上并排冲向终点。

branches.en: Striving for a shared goal is the root sense.
branches.cn: 为共同目标而努力，是这个词的词根义。

branches.en: A contest is the same striving with rules added.
branches.cn: 比赛就是同样的争胜加上了规则。

branches.en: Shops and runners both want to finish first.
branches.cn: 商店与跑者都想第一个到达。

branches.en: The word needs a rival; nobody competes alone.
branches.cn: 这个词需要一个对手；没有人独自竞争。

branches.en: To compete in an event is to accept its rules.
branches.cn: 参加一项比赛，就是接受它的规则。

intro.en: Compete is built on Latin com, together, plus petere, to seek.
intro.cn: compete 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 petere（追求）构成。

latinIntro.en: The seeking base pet- also appears in appetite and petition.
latinIntro.cn: 表示追求的词基 pet- 也出现在 appetite 与 petition 里。

items.example: The team competed in three cities.
items.exampleCN: 这支队伍在三座城市参赛。

items.example: The two are competing for the same buyers.
items.exampleCN: 两家在争夺同一批买家。

items.meaning: a person or firm you compete with
items.example: Our main competitor cut its prices.
items.exampleCN: 我们的主要对手降价了。
训练提高了队伍的竞争力。

definition_zh: 能力；胜任力；权限；（语言）能力
definition_en: the ability to do a task well enough, or the official power to act in a matter
core_image: 一位法官坐在案前，手边摊着法条与案卷，桌角立着一支笔
scene: 法庭先要确认自己对这桩纠纷是否有审理权，再进入实体审理。The court questioned its own competence to hear the case.
sceneCN: 法庭先确认对这桩纠纷是否有审理权，才进入实体审理；句中的 competence 指「官方权限」（第 2 个义项：依法可以管辖某事的权力）。图中可辨识物件：法条、案卷、法官席、笔。

pos.zh: 能力；胜任力；权限；（语言）能力

senses.title: Ability to do a job well enough
senses.titleCN: 足以把工作做好的能力
senses.definition: the ability to carry out a task to an acceptable standard
senses.definitionCN: 把一项任务做到可接受标准的能力
senses.example: The exam tests competence rather than memorised facts.
senses.exampleCN: 这项考试检验的是胜任能力，而非背下来的事实。
senses.why: competere meant 'to meet, to come together, to be suitable', so competence is the point at which a person and a task meet properly.
senses.whyCN: competere 意为「相遇、相合、适合」，因此 competence 就是人与任务恰好相合的那个点。

senses.title: Official power to act
senses.definition: the legal authority of a body or an official to decide a matter
senses.definitionCN: 机构或官员对某事作出决定的法定权力
senses.example: The court questioned its own competence to hear the case.
senses.exampleCN: 法院对自身审理此案的权限提出疑问。
senses.why: law took the 'suitability' sense and made it formal: a court is competent when the matter properly belongs to it.
senses.whyCN: 法律取用「相合」义并使之形式化：当某事正属某一法院管辖，该法院即有权限。

senses.title: Knowledge of language rules
senses.definition: the underlying knowledge a speaker has of a language's rules
senses.definitionCN: 说话者对一种语言规则的内在知识
senses.example: Linguistic competence is not the same as what a speaker actually says.
senses.exampleCN: 语言能力并不等同于说话者实际说出的内容。
senses.why: linguistics borrowed the word for hidden knowledge, contrasting it with performance, the actual use of that knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借这个词指隐藏的知识，并与「实际运用」相区分。

senses.title: The skill set a role requires
senses.definition: the set of skills and behaviours a position demands
senses.definitionCN: 某一职位所要求的一组技能与行为
senses.example: The job description lists the competences required for the role.
senses.exampleCN: 职位说明列出了该岗位所需的能力项。
senses.why: when employers list competences, they break competence into named pieces that can be taught and checked.
senses.whyCN: 雇主列出「能力项」时，是把胜任力拆成可教、可查的具名部件。

senses.title: Organisational capability
senses.definition: the collective ability of an institution to deliver what it promises
senses.definitionCN: 机构兑现承诺的整体能力
senses.example: The audit judged the agency's competence in emergency planning.
senses.exampleCN: 审计评估了该机构在应急规划方面的能力。
senses.why: the unit can rise from a person to an organisation, and competence then means the whole body's capacity to deliver.
senses.whyCN: 单位可以从个人上升到组织，competence 也就指整个机构交付的能力。

senses.title: Sufficiency of means
senses.titleCN: 财力物力上的足够（旧义）
senses.definition: enough income or resources to live or to act, an older legal and everyday sense
senses.definitionCN: 足以生活或行事的收入与资源，属较旧的法律与日常义
senses.example: The estate was valued as sufficient for her competence.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业被估定为足以维持她的生活。
senses.why: the oldest everyday sense was 'means sufficient for living', which survives in legal wording about a person's estate.
senses.whyCN: 最早的日常义是「足以维持生活的财产」，这一意义残留在关于个人财产的法律措辞中。

senses.title: A professional standard
senses.definition: the level of skill a profession regards as safe to practise
senses.definitionCN: 行业视为可以安全执业的技能水平
senses.example: The board found him below the competence required for surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会认定他未达到外科所要求的胜任水平。
senses.why: professions define competence as a floor, not a ceiling: below it, practice is unsafe.
senses.whyCN: 行业把胜任力定义为地板而非天花板：低于它，执业就不安全。

senses.title: Fitness to function, in old biology
senses.titleCN: 旧生物学：机能上的适应
senses.definition: the ability of an organism or organ to function as its kind should
senses.definitionCN: 生物体或器官按其种类应有的运作能力
senses.example: Early texts spoke of the competence of the organ to repair itself.
senses.exampleCN: 早期文献谈到该器官自我修复的机能。
senses.why: older biology used the word for an organ's fitness, the same 'suitability' idea applied to living tissue.
senses.whyCN: 较早的生物学用这个词指器官的适应能力，仍是那套「相合」观念用在活体组织上。

intro.en: Competence comes from Latin competentia 'a meeting, agreement', built on competere 'to meet, come together, be suitable', from com- 'together' and petere 'to seek, aim at'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competence 来自拉丁 competentia「相遇、一致」，由 competere「相遇、相合、适合」构成，后者又由 com-「共同」与 petere「寻求、指向」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Petere meant 'to seek, to aim at, to attack'. It is also the root of petition, appetite and repeat, all built on the idea of aiming toward something.
items.cn: petere 意为「寻求、指向、攻击」，也是 petition、appetite 与 repeat 的词根，这些词都建立在「朝某物指向」的观念上。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus petere gave competere 'to meet, to fall together, to be suitable or sufficient'. Two people seeking the same prize also competed.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 petere 给出 competere「相遇、相合、合适或足够」。两人争同一奖品，也就是「竞争」。

items.en: Competentia named a meeting or a correspondence between things, hence a proper fit between a person and a duty.
items.cn: competentia 指事物之间的相遇或对应，因此也指人与职责之间恰当的相合。

items.en: English took competence in the sixteenth century for the power or ability to act, including legal authority.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 competence，指行动的能力或权力，包括法定权限。

items.en: In the twentieth century linguistics gave the word a technical sense: the hidden knowledge of rules that makes speech possible, set against actual performance.
items.cn: 二十世纪语言学给了这个词一个术语义：使言语成为可能的、关于规则的内在知识，与实际的言语运用相对。

items.en: The deeper origin of petere is uncertain; the common link to a root meaning 'to rush at' is a reconstruction. The relation between competere and competere 'to compete' is historical but the modern split in meaning is not documented step by step.
items.cn: petere 的更早来源不确定；常被提到的、与表示「扑向」的词根的联系属重构形式。competere 与「竞争」义的关系是历史事实，但现代语义的分化缺乏逐步记录。

note.en: Group one holds the same Latin root under neighbouring spellings, including one that now means something quite different; group two holds words for ability that differ in scope and in legal force.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词根、拼写相邻的词，其中有的今义已大不相同；第二组是表示能力的词，范围与法律效力各不相同。

entries.definition: Describes a person or body that has the ability or the authority; competence is the noun for that ability.
entries.definitionCN: 描述有能力或有权限的人或机构；competence 是表示这种能力的名词。

entries.definition: Usually a single skill or behaviour standard, especially in human resources; competence is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 通常指单项技能或行为标准，多用于人力资源；competence 更宽。

entries.definition: From the same verb, but names the contest of people aiming at one prize, not the ability to do a job.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该动词，但指众人争同一奖品的竞赛，而非做好工作的能力。

entries.definition: From petere 'to seek': a formal request. It shares the root but not the prefix, and has nothing to do with ability.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 petere「寻求」：正式请求。同词根而不同前缀，与能力无关。

entries.definition: The general word for being able; competence adds the idea of meeting a standard or a duty.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「能够」的通用词；competence 多出「达到标准或职责要求」之意。

entries.definition: Often about potential capacity, of a person or a system, including what could be developed.
entries.definitionCN: 常指人或系统的潜在容量，包括尚可发展出来的部分。

entries.definition: A specific learned technique; competence is the overall fitness to perform a role.
entries.definitionCN: 指具体学成的技术；competence 是整体上能胜任一个角色。

entries.definition: The legal word for the power to decide, close to the legal sense of competence but more explicit.
entries.definitionCN: 表示裁决权的法律用词，接近 competence 的权限义但更明确。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real meeting image in competere, the real legal sense and the real modern split from competition.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自 competere 真实的「相遇」意象、真实的权限义，以及它与「竞争」的真实现代分化。

normal.en: com- 'together' plus petere 'seek': two things seeking and meeting, hence fitting.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 petere「寻求」：两物相寻而相遇，因此相合。

normal.en: The same verb also gives competition: two people seeking one prize.
normal.cn: 同一动词也给出 competition：两人争一个奖品。

normal.en: Legal competence means the matter belongs to your court.
normal.cn: 法律上的权限意味着这件事归你这家法院管。

normal.en: Linguistic competence is hidden knowledge, contrasted with actual performance.
normal.cn: 语言能力是隐藏的知识，与实际的言语运用相对。

normal.en: Employers pluralise it into competences: teachable named skills.
normal.cn: 雇主把它变成复数「能力项」：可教的具名技能。

abstract.en: Picture two puzzle pieces that meet exactly, neither forced nor loose.
abstract.cn: 想象两块拼图恰好合上，既不勉强也不松动。

abstract.en: Picture a key that fits one lock and no other.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙只能开一把锁。

abstract.en: Picture a floor line in a workshop below which nobody may work alone.
abstract.cn: 想象车间地面画着一条线，线下不许独自作业。

examples.en: The role requires competence in both accounting and law.
examples.cn: 这个岗位要求兼具会计与法律方面的能力。

examples.en: The tribunal has competence over disputes of this kind.
examples.cn: 该法庭对这类纠纷有管辖权。

examples.en: Her competence was never in doubt, only her authority.
examples.cn: 她的能力从不受疑，受疑的只是她的权限。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「com（共同）+ pet（追求）」——人与事恰好相合 → 能力、胜任、权限

root: 拉丁 com-「共同」+ petere「寻求、指向」→ competere「相遇、相合、适合」→ competentia「相遇、一致」→ 英语 competence；petere 的更早来源不确定，与「扑向」词根的联系属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn on one meeting: a person and a duty come together and fit, and that fit is then read as ability, as legal power, as hidden language knowledge, as a named skill, as institutional capacity, as old means of living, as a professional floor and as an organ's fitness.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次「相遇」转动：人与职责走到一起并恰好相合；这份相合随后被读成能力、法定权限、隐藏的语言知识、具名技能、机构容量、旧时的生活财力、职业地板与器官的适应力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pieces meeting exactly, a key and its one lock, a fit that is neither forced nor loose.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块拼图恰好合上，一把钥匙与唯一那把锁，一种既不勉强也不松动的相合。

branches.en: FIT FOR WORK: the meeting of person and task, whether judged whole or broken into named skills.
branches.cn: 与工作相合：人与任务的相遇，或整体评判，或拆成具名技能。

branches.en: POWER AND FLOOR: law formalises the fit as jurisdiction, and a profession fixes it as a minimum.
branches.cn: 权力与地板：法律把相合形式化为权限，行业把它固定为下限。

branches.en: HIDDEN RULES: linguistics reads the fit as knowledge behind speech rather than speech itself.
branches.cn: 隐藏规则：语言学把相合读成言语背后的知识，而非言语本身。

branches.en: THE BODY: the same fit scales up from a person to an institution that must deliver.
branches.cn: 整体：同一份相合从个人放大到必须交付的机构。

branches.en: OLD SENSES: enough means to live, and an organ fit to function, both kept from earlier usage.
branches.cn: 旧义：足以生活的财力与足以运作的器官，两者都从更早用法留存。

intro.en: The noun is a Latin prefix, root and suffix, and the same pieces build the whole competent family, including the branch that became competition.
intro.cn: 这个名词由拉丁前缀、词根与后缀构成，同一批部件造出整个 competent 词族，其中包括分出去成为 competition 的那一支。

latinIntro.en: Com- and petere build competere; its participle competens gives competent, and competentia gives the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: com- 与 petere 构成 competere；其分词 competens 给出 competent，competentia 给出英语名词。

items.example: The prefix brings the two sides together.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把两方带到一起。

items.meaningCN: 适合的；有能力的；有权限的

items.example: Competence is the noun of state.
Competency is common in human resources.

items.meaning: a seeking together for one prize

definition_zh: 有能力的；胜任的；合格的
definition_en: having enough skill or knowledge to do something properly
core_image: 工匠一手扶住木料，一手稳稳下刀，不多不少
scene: 新来的电工查了一遍线路，十几分钟就排除了故障。She is competent enough to handle the job alone.
sceneCN: 这里 competent 指「有能力的；胜任的」（第 1 个义项：具备足够本领）；句意是她足以独立处理这项工作。

pos.zh: 有能力的；胜任的；合格的

senses.title: Skilled enough to do the job
senses.definition: having enough skill or knowledge for a task
senses.definitionCN: 具备完成任务所需的技能或知识
senses.example: She is a competent driver on mountain roads.
senses.exampleCN: 她在山路上是个称职的司机。
senses.why: The word asks one quiet question: can this person carry the task safely?
senses.whyCN: 这个词只问一个朴素的问题：这人能把事稳妥地担起来吗。

senses.title: Acceptable but not outstanding
senses.definition: good enough to be accepted, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 足以被接受，但算不上出色
senses.example: The report is competent but never exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告合格，却谈不上精彩。
senses.why: Once a bar is set, meeting it exactly can sound like faint praise.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了及格线，刚刚够到就会带一点勉强的称赞。

intro.en: Competent comes from Latin competere, which also meant to be fit for a task.
intro.cn: competent 来自拉丁语 competere，这个词也有「适合某项任务」的意思。

items.en: Petere meant to seek or to aim at.
items.cn: petere 意为追求或瞄准。

items.en: Competere could mean to be suitable for something.
items.cn: competere 可以表示适合某事。

items.en: Competens described a person equal to a duty.
items.cn: competens 描述能担起职责的人。

items.en: Old French competent kept the sense of being fit.
items.cn: 古法语 competent 保留了「合适、称职」的含义。

items.en: English competent settled into skill and legal fitness.
items.cn: 英语 competent 落在技能与法律资格两方面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds members of the compete family, and the meaning group ranks capable, qualified and merely skilled.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 compete 家族的成员，近义组分辨有能力的、合格的和只是熟练的。

entries.definition: having the right training or papers

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a steady knife, then move to the standard a task sets and to the mild praise of just meeting it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从稳稳的一刀开始，再走到任务设定的标准以及刚刚够格时那点温和的称赞。

normal.en: Competent shares a root with compete: you are fit for the task at hand.
normal.cn: competent 与 compete 同根：你对眼前这件事是够格的。

normal.en: Competent is about the bar, not about brilliance.
normal.cn: competent 说的是及格线，而不是出众。

normal.en: The noun is competence, and its opposite is incompetence.
normal.cn: 名词是 competence，反面就是 incompetence。

normal.en: A competent cook never burns the rice.
normal.cn: 一个称职的厨子不会把米饭烧糊。

normal.en: Competent at a task means you can be trusted with it.
normal.cn: competent at 一项任务，意味着这件事可以交给你。

abstract.en: Picture a knife following a pencilled line without slipping.
abstract.cn: 想象一刀顺着铅笔线走，没有偏。

abstract.en: Picture a driver checking the mirror before changing lanes.
abstract.cn: 想象司机变道前先看一眼后视镜。

abstract.en: Picture a bar just touched by a jumper's hand.
abstract.cn: 想象跳高者的手刚好碰到横杆。

examples.en: A competent mechanic can find the fault quickly.
examples.cn: 一个有能力的技工能很快找出故障。

examples.en: The team is competent at handling complaints.
examples.cn: 这个团队处理投诉很在行。

examples.en: Her work is competent rather than brilliant.
examples.cn: 她的工作合格，但算不上出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 competent 记成 com（一起）加 pet（追求）加 ent：追得上任务要求的人，就是有能力的。

root: 源自拉丁语 competere，本义是「足以相称、合乎要求」，后指具备足够本领的、胜任的。

sensesIntro.en: From having the skill a task demands, to just meeting the bar and no more.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拥有任务所需的技能，到刚好够上及格线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carpenter whose knife follows the line without slipping.
core.cn: 核心意象：工匠一手扶住木料，一手稳稳下刀，不多不少。

branches.en: Being fit for the task is the practical core.
branches.cn: 足以胜任任务是这个词务实的核心。

branches.en: Meeting the bar exactly can sound like faint praise.
branches.cn: 刚好够到及格线，听起来就像淡淡的称赞。

branches.en: Both senses measure a person against a standard.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是拿一个人去对照一个标准。

branches.en: Trust grows when skill can be relied on.
branches.cn: 本领可靠，信任才会生长。

branches.en: The second sense warns against stopping at good enough.
branches.cn: 第二个义项提醒人别停在「够用」上。

intro.en: Competent takes the Latin base compet- and the adjective ending -ent.
intro.cn: competent 由拉丁词基 compet- 加形容词后缀 -ent 构成。

latinIntro.en: The same base yields competence, competent and competition.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个词基产出 competence、competent 与 competition。

items.meaning: the ability to do something well
items.example: Her competence reassured the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 她的能力让整个团队安心。

items.meaning: a specific skill needed for a job
items.example: The job lists five core competencies.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作列出五项核心能力。

items.meaning: in a skilled and reliable way
items.exampleCN: 她称职地处理了这个案子。

items.meaning: not skilled enough for a task
items.example: An incompetent pilot is a danger.
items.exampleCN: 不称职的飞行员是一种危险。

items.meaning: lack of skill for a task
items.exampleCN: 报告把原因归为纯粹的不称职。
这次修理做得极不专业。

items.example: Managers need both technical and social competencies.
items.exampleCN: 管理者既需要技术专长，也需要社交能力。

definition_zh: 比赛；竞争；竞争对手
definition_en: an event in which people try to win, or the rivalry between people or firms who want the same thing
core_image: 几条船挤在同一条起跑线上，桨叶同时入水
scene: 报名表贴出三天，走廊里已经挤满了准备参赛的学生。The competition attracted students from twenty schools.
sceneCN: 这里 competition 指「比赛」（第 1 个义项：争夺名次的活动）；句意是这场比赛吸引了二十所学校的学生。

senses.title: A contest
senses.definition: an event in which people try to win a prize
senses.definitionCN: 人们争夺奖项的活动
senses.example: She won the writing competition at school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校作文比赛中获奖。
senses.why: A fixed event with rules turns rivalry into something you can watch and score.
senses.whyCN: 有规则、有场地的活动，把争胜变成看得见、可评分的事。

senses.title: Rivalry between people or firms
senses.definition: the struggle between people or companies for the same aim
senses.definitionCN: 人或公司为同一目标而进行的争夺
senses.example: Price competition keeps the market healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 价格竞争让市场保持健康。
senses.why: The same striving continues without a referee, in shops and offices.
senses.whyCN: 同样的争胜在没有裁判的商店与办公室里继续。

senses.title: The rivals themselves
senses.definition: the people or firms you are trying to beat
senses.definitionCN: 你想要胜过的那些人或公司
senses.example: The competition has cut its prices again.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争对手又降价了。
senses.why: By a small shift, the contest comes to mean the other side in it.
senses.whyCN: 词义轻轻一转，比赛就指比赛里的对方。

intro.en: Competition comes from Latin competitio, the noun of competere, to seek the same thing together.
intro.cn: competition 来自拉丁语 competitio，是 competere（一起追求同一目标）的名词形式。

items.en: Competere meant to seek the same prize as another.
items.cn: competere 意为与别人追求同一个奖赏。

items.en: Competitio named the shared striving itself.
items.cn: competitio 指这种共同的争求本身。

items.en: It also described a legal claim between two parties.
items.cn: 它也描述两方之间的法律争讼。

items.en: Old French competition narrowed to contests and trade.
items.cn: 古法语 competition 收窄到比赛与商业。

items.en: English competition covered sport, markets and rival firms.
items.cn: 英语 competition 覆盖体育、市场与对手公司。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other -tion nouns easily confused with competition, and the meaning group separates a contest, a rivalry and a match.
note.cn: 形近组收的是容易与 competition 混淆的其他名词，近义组分辨竞赛、对抗与一场比赛。

entries.definition: an event where people try to win

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with boats on one line, then move to the everyday struggle and to the rivals on the other side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从同一条起跑线上的船开始，再走到日常的争夺以及对面的对手。

normal.en: Competition is the noun behind compete: it names the whole scene.
normal.cn: competition 是 compete 背后的名词：它给整个场面命名。

normal.en: Enter a competition, win a competition, but feel competition in a market.
normal.cn: 可以说参加比赛、赢得比赛，也会在市场里感受到竞争。

normal.en: Fierce competition is the phrase shops use when prices fall.
normal.cn: 降价时商家会说竞争激烈，用的就是 fierce competition。

normal.en: The competition can also be the other team, not the event.
normal.cn: the competition 也可以指对方队伍，而不是那场活动。

normal.en: A competitor is one person; competition is the whole field.
normal.cn: competitor 是一个人，competition 是整个赛场。

abstract.en: Picture five oars hitting the water at the same second.
abstract.cn: 想象五支桨在同一秒入水。

abstract.en: Picture two price boards changing in the same street.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条街上两块价目牌先后更换。

abstract.en: Picture a judge holding a list of names and a stopwatch.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判拿着名单和秒表。

examples.en: The design competition drew over a hundred entries.
examples.cn: 这次设计比赛收到一百多件作品。

examples.en: Fierce competition forced the shop to close.
examples.cn: 激烈的竞争迫使这家店关门。

examples.en: Our competition launched a cheaper model.
examples.cn: 我们的竞争对手推出了一款更便宜的型号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 competition 记成 com（一起）加 pet（追求）加 ition：一群人一起追同一个奖品，就是竞争与比赛。

root: 源自拉丁语 competitio，由 competere（一起追求）加名词后缀而来，本义是共同争求同一目标，后指比赛、竞争与对手。

sensesIntro.en: From a scored contest, to the everyday struggle, and finally to the rivals in it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从计分的比赛，到日常的争夺，最后到争夺中的对手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several boats pressed against one starting line, oars entering the water at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：几条船挤在同一条起跑线上，桨叶同时入水。

branches.en: The scored event is the clearest sense of competition.
branches.cn: 计分的赛事是 competition 最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Without rules, the same striving becomes market rivalry.
branches.cn: 没有规则时，同样的争胜就成了市场竞争。

branches.en: The contest can stand for the other side in it.
branches.cn: 比赛可以代指比赛里的另一方。

branches.en: Both are one prize chased by many hands.
branches.cn: 两者都是许多只手去追同一个奖赏。

branches.en: In business the rivals are the competition.
branches.cn: 在生意里，对手就是 the competition。

intro.en: Competition joins the verb compete with the noun ending -ition.
intro.cn: competition 由动词 compete 加名词后缀 -ition 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin petere, to seek, is the small engine inside the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 petere（追求）是整个词族内部的小引擎。

items.example: The school holds three competitions a year.
items.exampleCN: 学校每年举办三场比赛。

items.example: They compete for the same buyers.
Two competing plans were on the table.
items.exampleCN: 桌上有两个相互竞争方案。

items.meaning: eager to win or able to win
items.example: The firm stays competitive by cutting costs.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司靠削减成本保持竞争力。
每位参赛者都戴着一个号码。
这个指数衡量经济竞争力。

definition_zh: 竞争者；竞争对手；参赛者
definition_en: a person, firm or team that competes with another for the same customers, prize or resource
core_image: 两条跑道并排，两个人影在同一终点线前加速，观众只看谁先到
scene: 赛道边，两辆赛车并排冲过弯道，维修区里的人盯着计时屏。A smaller competitor undercut the leader by cutting its delivery times.
sceneCN: 这里 competitor 指「在同一市场中争夺顾客的对手」（第 1 个义项：与企业争夺同一批顾客的另一家企业）；句意为一家规模较小的竞争者通过缩短交货时间压过了领先者。图中可辨识物件：并排的两辆赛车、计时屏、维修区、终点线。

pos.zh: 竞争者；竞争对手；参赛者

senses.title: A firm chasing the same customers
senses.titleCN: 争夺同一批顾客的企业
senses.definition: a business that sells goods or services to the same buyers as another business
senses.definitionCN: 与另一家企业面向同一批买主出售商品或服务的企业
senses.example: The two competitors cut prices within a week of each other.
senses.exampleCN: 两家竞争对手在一周之内先后降价。
senses.why: the Latin verb meant 'to seek together', so a competitor is literally one who seeks the same thing alongside others.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「一起寻求」，因此 competitor 字面上就是与他人一起寻求同一样东西的人。

senses.title: An athlete or team in a contest
senses.definition: a person or team taking part in a sporting or academic contest
senses.definitionCN: 参加体育或学术比赛的选手或队伍
senses.example: She beat three competitors to win the regional final.
senses.exampleCN: 她击败三名参赛者，赢得地区决赛。
senses.why: sport kept the oldest sense: people striving for one prize on the same field.
senses.whyCN: 体育保留了最古老的义项：在同一场地上争夺同一个奖赏的人。

senses.title: A rival for a post or place
senses.titleCN: 竞聘职位或名额的对手
senses.definition: a person who applies for the same job, school place or grant
senses.definitionCN: 申请同一职位、学位名额或资助的人
senses.example: Six competitors were shortlisted for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 有六名竞争者进入了该职位的候选名单。
senses.why: the same 'seeking together' structure applies whenever a limited number of places is on offer.
senses.whyCN: 只要名额有限，「一起寻求」的结构就同样适用。

senses.title: A substitute product or technology
senses.definition: a product or technology that can take the place of another in the buyer's use
senses.definitionCN: 在买主的使用中能取代另一产品的产品或技术
senses.example: Rail travel is a competitor to short-haul flights.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路出行是短途航班的竞争者。
senses.why: economists widened the term because a rival need not sell the same thing, only serve the same need.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家扩大了这个词的用法，因为对手不必卖同样的东西，只需满足同样的需求。

senses.title: A species rival in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中争夺资源的物种
senses.definition: an organism that uses the same limited resource as another species or individual
senses.definitionCN: 与另一物种或个体使用同一种有限资源的生物
senses.example: The two bird species are competitors for the same nesting holes.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种鸟是同一批筑巢洞的竞争者。
senses.why: ecology borrowed the market word because both describe a scramble for a fixed supply.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用了市场用语，因为两者都描述对固定供给的争夺。

senses.title: An atom-like firm in a market model
senses.titleCN: 市场模型中的原子式厂商
senses.definition: one of many small sellers in a model where no single one can affect price
senses.definitionCN: 在没有任何单一卖方能影响价格的模型中，众多小卖方之一
senses.example: In perfect competition no competitor can move the market price alone.
senses.exampleCN: 在完全竞争中，没有哪个竞争者能单独左右市场价格。
senses.why: the economics textbook makes the competitor small by definition, so the word loses its sense of threat.
senses.whyCN: 经济学教科书按定义把竞争者设得很小，于是这个词失去了威胁意味。

senses.title: A potential entrant not yet selling
senses.titleCN: 尚未开卖但可能进入的对手
senses.definition: a firm that could enter the market and constrain incumbents even before it does
senses.definitionCN: 可能进入市场、甚至在进入前就约束现有企业的企业
senses.example: A new entrant can be a competitor before it opens a single store.
senses.exampleCN: 新进入者在开第一家店之前就已是竞争者。
senses.why: antitrust counts potential entry because the threat of a competitor can discipline prices.
senses.whyCN: 反垄断把潜在进入计入，因为竞争者的威胁就能约束价格。

senses.title: Any party seeking the same scarce thing
senses.titleCN: 任何争夺同一稀缺资源的方
senses.definition: a person, group or institution pursuing the same limited fund, attention or territory
senses.definitionCN: 追逐同一有限资金、注意力或领地的人、群体或机构
senses.example: Two charities became competitors for the same donation pool.
senses.exampleCN: 两家慈善机构成了同一笔捐款池的竞争者。
senses.why: the word generalizes once 'seeking together' is detached from shops and prizes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「一起寻求」脱离商店与奖赏，这个词就一般化了。

intro.en: Competitor is Latin competitor 'one who strives with another', from competere, built on com- 'together' and petere 'to seek, aim at'. Petere also gives petition and appetite. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competitor 来自拉丁 competitor「与他人相争的人」，其动词 competere 由 com-「共同」与 petere「寻求、瞄准」构成。petere 还衍生 petition 与 appetite。年代均为约数。

items.en: Petere meant 'to seek, head for, attack'. Petition and appetite descend from the same verb, one asking and one reaching for food.
items.cn: petere 意为「寻求、前往、攻击」。petition 与 appetite 都出自同一动词，一个表示请求，一个表示对食物的欲求。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus petere produced competere 'to seek together, strive jointly', and in legal use 'to claim jointly'.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 petere 构成 competere「一起寻求、共同力争」，在法律用语中指「共同主张」。

items.en: The noun competitor named the person who strives alongside another for the same object; English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 competitor 指与他人为同一目标相争的人；英语在 16 世纪借入。

items.en: Competere also meant 'to be fit or proper for', which produced competent and competence; that branch shares the verb but not the rivalry.
items.cn: competere 还表示「适合、相称」，由此产生 competent 与 competence；这一支共享动词，却不含相争之义。

items.en: From the nineteenth century competitor became a standard word for a firm in a market, and competition law gave it a technical edge.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，competitor 成为市场中企业的标准称法，竞争法又赋予它技术性含义。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. The deeper origin of petere is reconstructed rather than demonstrated.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。petere 的更深来源属重构形式，并非已证形式。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin verb that are easy to confuse with the rival noun; group two holds near synonyms for the person or side one is up against.
note.cn: 第一组是同出那个拉丁动词、易与「对手」名词混淆的词；第二组是表示「所面对的人或一方」的近义词。

entries.definition: The activity or event of competing; a competitor is a participant, while competition is what they take part in.
entries.definitionCN: 竞争这一活动或赛事；competitor 是参与者，competition 是他们参与的那件事。

entries.definition: Describing a person, price or market that is able to compete; it qualifies the contest rather than naming a rival.
entries.definitionCN: 形容有能力竞争的人、价格或市场；它修饰竞争，而非指称对手。

entries.definition: From the 'be fit for' branch of competere, meaning capable or legally qualified; it has nothing to do with rivalry.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 competere 的「适合」一支，意为有能力或法律上合格的；与相争无关。

entries.definition: One who presents a petition, from petere 'seek'; a petitioner seeks a decision, not a customer.
entries.definitionCN: 提交请愿书的人，出自 petere「寻求」；请愿者寻求的是裁决，不是顾客。

entries.definition: From Latin rivalis, one who draws water from the same stream; it stresses a continuing contest between two sides.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 rivalis，指同一条溪流取水的人；强调双方持续相争的关系。

entries.definition: The person or team on the other side of a contest; it fits sport and debate better than markets.
entries.definitionCN: 比赛或辩论中站在对面的人或队伍；比用于市场更贴合体育与辩论。

entries.definition: An opponent seen as an enemy; it adds hostility that competitor, a neutral market word, does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为敌人的对手；它增添了敌意，而中性的 market 用词 competitor 并不带这层意思。

entries.definition: A person or firm that enters a market or contest; an entrant becomes a competitor once it actually takes part.
entries.definitionCN: 进入市场或比赛的个人或企业；进入者真正参与后才成为竞争者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: com- 'together' + petere 'seek': one who seeks the same thing alongside you.
normal.cn: com-「共同」+ petere「寻求」：与你一起寻求同一样东西的人。

normal.en: The family runs compete, competition, competitive, competitiveness, competing, competitor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 compete、competition、competitive、competitiveness、competing、competitor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: main competitor, direct competitor, competitor analysis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：主要对手、直接对手、对手分析。

normal.en: Competent looks like a twin but came from the 'be fit for' branch of the same verb.
normal.cn: competent 看似同出一源，却来自同一动词的「适合」一支。

normal.en: Sports writing uses the same word for a runner, a team or a chess player.
normal.cn: 体育写作也用同一个词指跑者、队伍或棋手。

abstract.en: Picture two runners reaching for the same ribbon at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者在同一瞬间伸手去抓同一条终点带。

abstract.en: Picture two shops on one street watching each other's price tags.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条街上的两家店互相盯着对方的价签。

abstract.en: Picture two birds inspecting the same hole in a tree.
abstract.cn: 想象两只鸟查看着树上的同一个洞。

examples.en: The incumbent lost a third of its share to a foreign competitor.
examples.cn: 原有企业把三分之一的市场份额丢给了一家外国竞争者。

examples.en: A competitor's failure can be as dangerous as its success.
examples.cn: 对手的失败可能与它的成功一样危险。

examples.en: Every competitor in the race had to pass the same drug test.
examples.cn: 这场比赛的每位参赛者都必须通过同一项药检。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of seeking: someone aims at the same object as another, and that aim is then seen in a shop, on a track, at a job interview, in a substitute product, in a habitat, in an economic model, before entry, and in any scramble for a scarce thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「寻求」动作展开：某人与另一人瞄准同一目标，这个瞄准再依次出现在商店、跑道、求职、替代产品、栖息地、经济模型、进入之前，以及任何对稀缺物的争夺中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two runners side by side, both reaching for one ribbon.
core.cn: 核心意象：两名跑者并排，同伸一只手去抓同一条终点带。

branches.en: MARKET AND SUBSTITUTE: the firm chasing the same buyer, and the product that serves the same need.
branches.cn: 市场与替代：追逐同一买主的企业，以及满足同一需求的产品。

branches.en: PEOPLE IN CONTESTS: a runner on a track and an applicant on a shortlist.
branches.cn: 竞赛中的人：跑道上的选手与候选名单上的申请者。

branches.en: SPECIES IN A HABITAT: the same scramble transposed to nesting holes.
branches.cn: 栖息地中的物种：同一种争夺被移用到筑巢洞上。

branches.en: MODEL AND THREAT: an atom in a textbook market, and a firm that has not entered yet.
branches.cn: 模型与威胁：教科书市场里的原子，以及尚未进入的企业。

branches.en: ANY SCARCE PRIZE: charities, parties or families seeking one limited pool.
branches.cn: 任何稀缺奖赏：慈善机构、政党或家庭争夺同一个有限资源池。

intro.en: Competitor is a Latin noun whose verb is still productive in English, so the whole family can be read from com-, petere and the agent suffix.
intro.cn: competitor 是一个拉丁名词，其动词在英语中仍能产，因此整个词族可从 com-、petere 与施事后缀读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin petere supplies compete, competition, competitor and petition; com- marks the shared aim, and -or marks the person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 petere 提供 compete、competition、competitor 与 petition；com- 标记共同目标，-or 标记人。

definition_zh: 编纂；汇编；收集整理；（计算机）编译
definition_en: to gather material together into a book, list or file; to translate source code into machine instructions
core_image: 一摞散页被按页码收进同一只硬壳夹
scene: 编辑桌上摊着几十封信，她把它们按年份装进同一册。She spent a year compiling letters into a single volume.
sceneCN: 这里指把零散材料收集整理成一部作品（第 1 个义项：汇编成书）；句意是她花一年时间把信件汇编成一册。

pos.zh: 编纂；汇编；收集整理；编译

senses.title: To gather material into a book
senses.definition: to collect scattered writings and arrange them into one work
senses.definitionCN: 收集零散文字并编排成一部作品
senses.example: She compiled the letters into a single volume.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这些信件汇编成一册。
senses.why: Latin compilare meant to gather together, and book-making gave the gathering a finished shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 compilare 意为聚拢，制书让这种聚拢有了完成形态。

senses.title: To make a list
senses.definition: to draw up items in an ordered list
senses.definitionCN: 把条目按次序列成清单
senses.example: He compiled a list of every address in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 他编了一份全区地址清单。
senses.why: A list is the smallest finished form that gathering can take.
senses.whyCN: 清单是「聚拢」能取得的最小完成形态。

senses.title: To assemble data for use
senses.definition: to collect figures from many sources into one set
senses.definitionCN: 把多处数字汇集为一套
senses.example: The office compiled the figures before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室在会前汇总了这些数字。
senses.why: Modern administration gathers first and decides later.
senses.whyCN: 现代行政先汇集，后决定。

senses.title: To translate source code
senses.definition: to turn a program written by a person into instructions a machine can run
senses.definitionCN: 把人类写的程序转成机器能执行的指令
senses.example: The compiler turns each source file into an object file.
senses.exampleCN: 编译器把每个源文件转成目标文件。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the gathering word for a one-way translation into machine form.
senses.whyCN: 计算技术借这个「汇集」词，指单向转成机器形式。

senses.title: To collect evidence
senses.definition: to bring together documents and facts for an argument
senses.definitionCN: 为论证把文件与事实聚在一起
senses.example: The lawyer compiled the records into one file.
senses.exampleCN: 律师把这些记录汇入一个卷宗。
senses.why: The old sense of gathering without order survives in this use.
senses.whyCN: 古老的无序聚拢义在这种用法里仍然活着。

senses.title: To build an index or catalogue
senses.definition: to arrange entries so that each can be found
senses.definitionCN: 把条目编排到每一条都可查到
senses.example: The librarian compiled an index of the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 馆员为这批藏书编了索引。
senses.why: Order is added to the gathering, and the result is a finding tool.
senses.whyCN: 聚拢之上加了次序，结果就是检索工具。

senses.title: To draw up a report
senses.definition: to put gathered facts into a formal written account
senses.definitionCN: 把汇集的事实写成正式叙述
senses.example: The team compiled a report on the flood damage.
senses.exampleCN: 团队编写了一份洪灾损失报告。
senses.why: The word moves from collecting to composing without leaving the desk.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从收集走到撰写，始终没有离开书桌。

senses.title: To make an anthology
senses.definition: to choose pieces and arrange them as a collection
senses.definitionCN: 挑选篇目并编排成集
senses.example: The editor compiled an anthology of river poems.
senses.exampleCN: 编者编了一部河流诗选。
senses.why: Selection and arrangement are the two halves of compiling.
senses.whyCN: 挑选与编排是「编」的两半。

intro.en: Compile comes from Latin compilare, to gather together, perhaps also to plunder, from com- together plus pilare. The direct source is clear; the meaning of pilare in this compound is source uncertain.
intro.cn: compile 来自拉丁 compilare「聚拢」，也可能带「掠夺」义，由 com-「一起」与 pilare 构成。直接来源清楚；pilare 在这个复合词中的含义来源不确定。

items.en: Compilare meant to plunder, to gather together and to heap up, with the idea of things brought into one place.
items.cn: compilare 意为掠夺、聚拢、堆起，核心是把东西弄到一处。

items.en: Com- means together, and it supplies the collecting force of the verb.
items.cn: com- 意为一起，提供这个动词的收集力量。

items.en: Pilare is connected with pressing or plucking, but which of those senses belongs to this compound is source uncertain.
items.cn: pilare 与压、拔相关，但在此复合词中取哪一义，来源不确定。

items.en: Old French compiler narrowed the word to the gathering of writings.
items.cn: 古法语 compiler 把词义收窄到文字的汇集。

items.en: English took the verb in the late Middle Ages; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入这个动词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: In the 1950s the word was given to the translation of source code, which gathers programmes into machine form.
items.cn: 二十世纪五十年代，这个词被用于源代码翻译，即把程序汇集为机器形式。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin gathering stem; the second group names collecting and arranging.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「聚拢」词干；第二组是收集与编排的近义说法。

entries.definition: To bring things together, often without arranging them.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西聚到一起，常不含编排。

examples.en: She compiled a short list of the books worth keeping.

definition_zh: 抱怨；投诉；诉说
definition_en: to say that you are unhappy or not satisfied about something
core_image: 饭桌上有人皱着眉头把盘子往前一推
scene: 楼上整夜装修，邻居第二天一早就去了物业。She complained about the noise for a week.

senses.title: To say you are unhappy
senses.definition: to say that something is wrong or annoying
senses.definitionCN: 说出某事不对或令人烦
senses.example: He complained about the cold soup.
senses.exampleCN: 他抱怨汤是凉的。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply giving voice to a private displeasure.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项只是把心里的不快说出来。

senses.title: To make a formal protest
senses.definition: to tell an authority that something is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 向管理方说明某事有问题
senses.example: Guests complained to the manager about the room.
senses.exampleCN: 客人向经理投诉房间问题。
senses.why: When the listener has power to act, a complaint becomes a formal claim.
senses.whyCN: 当听者有权处理，抱怨就成了正式投诉。

senses.title: To describe a pain or illness
senses.definition: to say that you feel pain somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 说自己某处疼痛
senses.example: She complained of a headache all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她一上午都在说头痛。
senses.why: Pain, once spoken, becomes a symptom a doctor can read.
senses.whyCN: 疼痛一旦说出，就成了医生能读的症状。

items.en: English complain first meant to lament a loss.

items.en: It settled into grumbling, formal protest and naming a pain.

definition_zh: 补充物；补足；配套；（语法）补语；（数学）补集；（生物）补体
definition_en: something that completes another thing or makes it whole; to complete by adding what is missing
core_image: 一片拼图正好补进缺口，边线严丝合缝
scene: 餐桌上的深色桌布衬得浅色餐具更亮。The cool sauce is a complement to the rich meat.
sceneCN: 这里指补足他物、使其完整的东西（第 1 个义项：补足物）；句意为这清爽的酱汁与厚重的肉相配，正好补足。

pos.zh: 补充物；补足物；配套物；补语；补集；补体

senses.title: Something that completes another thing
senses.definition: a thing that supplies what another thing lacks
senses.definitionCN: 补上另一物所缺之物的东西
senses.example: The cool sauce is a complement to the rich meat.
senses.exampleCN: 这清爽的酱汁与厚重的肉相配。
senses.why: Complementum is that which fills up, from complere, to fill completely.
senses.whyCN: complementum 指把东西填满的部分，出自 complere「完全填满」。

senses.title: To complete by adding
senses.definition: to add what is needed to make something whole
senses.definitionCN: 加上所需之物使某事物完整
senses.example: The two parts complement each other.
senses.exampleCN: 这两部分相互补足。
senses.why: The verb turns the filling into an act performed by one thing on another.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「填满」变成一物对另一物施行的动作。

senses.title: A matched set
senses.definition: the full number needed for a set or a ship's crew
senses.definitionCN: 一个组合或一艘船所需的全额人数
senses.example: The ship sailed with its full complement of crew.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船载着全额船员出海。
senses.why: A set is complete when its count is filled, and the word marks that count.
senses.whyCN: 一个组合在人数填满时才算完整，这个词标记那个数额。

senses.title: A grammatical complement
senses.definition: a word or phrase that completes the meaning of a verb or subject
senses.definitionCN: 补足动词或主语意义的词或短语
senses.example: In the sentence she is a doctor, the noun is a complement.
senses.exampleCN: 在「她是一名医生」这句话里，那个名词是补语。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the filling image for the part that makes a clause whole.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借「填充」意象，指使从句完整的部分。

senses.title: A mathematical complement
senses.definition: the set of elements not in a given set
senses.definitionCN: 不属于某集合的元素所成的集合
senses.example: The complement of the odd numbers is the even numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 奇数的补集是偶数。
senses.why: Set theory asks what is left when a part is taken away, and calls it the filling of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 集合论问取走一部分后剩下什么，并把剩余称为补。

senses.title: A part of the immune system
senses.definition: a group of proteins that help antibodies destroy pathogens
senses.definitionCN: 协助抗体消灭病原体的一组蛋白
senses.example: The complement system marks the bacterium for destruction.
senses.exampleCN: 补体系统给细菌做上待清除的标记。
senses.why: The name was given because the proteins complete the work of antibodies.
senses.whyCN: 得名是因为这些蛋白完成抗体的工作。

senses.title: A colour opposite
senses.definition: a colour that sits opposite another on the colour wheel
senses.definitionCN: 色轮上与另一色相对的颜色
senses.example: Blue and orange are complementary colours.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝与橙是互补色。
senses.why: Two opposites complete a neutral balance, so the word fits the pair.
senses.whyCN: 两个相反色合成中性平衡，因此这个词适用于这一对。

senses.title: A logical complement
senses.definition: the negation or remainder of a proposition or class
senses.definitionCN: 命题或类别的否定或剩余
senses.example: The complement of the claim covers every other case.
senses.exampleCN: 这一说法的补覆盖其余所有情况。
senses.why: Logic uses the word for whatever the first statement leaves outside it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学用这个词指第一个陈述留在其外的一切。

intro.en: Complement comes from Latin complementum, that which fills up, from complere, to fill completely, built on com- together and plere, to fill. The direct source is clear.
intro.cn: complement 来自拉丁 complementum「用来填满之物」，出自 complere「完全填满」，由 com-「一起」与 plere「填」构成。直接来源清楚。

items.en: Plere meant to fill, and it also lies behind complete, supply and plenty.
items.cn: plere 意为填满，也藏在 complete、supply 与 plenty 背后。

items.en: Complere joined com- together with plere, giving the sense of filling something to the full.
items.cn: complere 把 com-「一起」与 plere 结合，给出「填到满」的意思。

items.en: Complementum was the part that did the filling, the thing needed to make a whole.
items.cn: complementum 指完成填充的那部分，即使整体成立所需之物。

items.en: French passed the word to English; the exact first English date is uncertain.
items.cn: 法语把这个词传给英语，英语确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Compliment reached English through French and Italian courtesy, and though both lines end at complere, the two words separated early.
items.cn: compliment 经法语与意大利语的礼节用法进入英语；两条线虽都止于 complere，词却很早分道。

items.en: Grammar, set theory, immunology and colour theory each name their missing piece a complement.
items.cn: 语法、集合论、免疫学与色彩理论都把自己缺的那一块叫作补。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin filling stem; the second group names things that complete or go well with another.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「填满」词干；第二组是补足或相配的近义说法。

entries.definition: Praise or a polite remark; a different word despite the closeness.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞或礼貌用语；虽形近却是另一个词。

entries.definition: Serving to complete or balance another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 起补足或平衡另一物作用的。

entries.definition: The act or process of completing.
Whole, with nothing missing; from the same filling verb.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的，什么都不缺；出自同一「填满」动词。

entries.definition: To provide what is needed; from supplere, to fill up.
entries.definitionCN: 提供所需之物；出自 supplere「填满」。

entries.definition: Something added to improve or extend, not to complete.
entries.definitionCN: 为改进或延长而添加之物，不是为补全。

entries.definition: A person or thing matching another in role.
entries.definitionCN: 在角色上与他者对应的人或物。

entries.definition: Something put in beside what is already there.
entries.definitionCN: 放到已有之物旁边的东西。

entries.definition: One of a pair that goes well with the other.
An even arrangement of opposite parts.
entries.definitionCN: 相反部分之间的均衡安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin filling verb, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「填满」动词、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Complere is to fill completely, so a complement is the piece that fills the gap.
normal.cn: complere 是完全填满，所以 complement 就是填缺口的那一块。

normal.en: Complement completes; supplement adds without necessarily completing.
normal.cn: complement 补全；supplement 添加，却未必补全。

normal.en: Compliment is praise, not completion, even though the two words look alike.
normal.cn: compliment 是称赞，不是补全，尽管两个词长得像。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: a complement to, full complement, complement each other.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：对…的补充、全额编制、相互补足。

normal.en: Set theory and immunology both name their missing piece a complement.
normal.cn: 集合论与免疫学都把自己缺的那一块叫补。

abstract.en: Complement is a puzzle piece whose edge fits exactly, making the picture whole.
abstract.cn: 补充是一块边线正吻合的拼图，让画面完整。

abstract.en: The word does not add more of the same; it adds what was missing.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是添加同类的更多，而是添加缺少的那一种。

abstract.en: Two opposite colours complete each other into grey.
abstract.cn: 两种相反色相互补足成灰。

examples.en: The two sisters have complementary talents but very different habits.
examples.cn: 两姐妹才能互补，习惯却大不相同。

examples.en: A full complement of officers reported for duty.
examples.cn: 全额军官报到履职。

examples.en: The wine complements the cheese without overpowering it.
examples.cn: 这款酒与奶酪相配，却不压过它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「康普力门特」——把缺的那块补齐：补充；补足物

root: 拉丁 complementum「用来填满之物」← complere「完全填满」← com-「一起」+ plere「填」。同族 complete、supply 同出 plere；compliment 经法语与意大利语礼节用法另成一路，虽同止于 complere 但很早分道。法语传入英语，确切首见年代不确定；语法、集合论、免疫学与色彩理论各有专义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fill a gap in table, theory, grammar, sets, immunity, colour, logic and a taste.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在餐桌、理论、语法、集合、免疫、色彩、逻辑与口味上填补缺口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a puzzle piece whose edge fits exactly, leaving no gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块边线严丝合缝的拼图，不留缺口。

branches.en: THE FILLING PIECE: the thing supplied and the act of supplying it.
branches.cn: 填充的那块：被补上的东西与补上的动作。

branches.en: THE FULL COUNT: a set or crew brought to its required number.
branches.cn: 全额：组合或船员达到所需人数。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE AND THE PROPOSITION: what completes a sentence and what the first claim leaves outside itself.
branches.cn: 从句与命题：使句子完整的部分，以及首个陈述留在其外的东西。

branches.en: THE SET REMAINDER: everything not in a given set.
branches.cn: 集合的剩余：不在给定集合中的一切。

branches.en: THE BALANCED PAIR: proteins completing antibodies and colours completing each other.
branches.cn: 平衡的一对：完成抗体工作的蛋白与彼此补足的两种颜色。

intro.en: Complement is the Latin filling noun and verb; plere is the core and com- adds the togetherness.
intro.cn: complement 是拉丁语「填满」的名词与动词；plere 是核心，com- 加上「一起」。

latinIntro.en: Plere supplies the fill, complementum the thing that fills, and complere the act; compliment is a separate courtesy line.
latinIntro.cn: plere 提供「填」，complementum 提供填充之物，complere 提供动作；compliment 是另一条礼节线。

items.example: The prefix makes the filling complete rather than partial.
items.exampleCN: 前缀使填充完全，而不是部分。

items.example: The verb is the core of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的核心。

items.structure: Latin verb from com- and plere
items.example: The compound adds the sense of reaching fullness.
items.exampleCN: 复合词加上「达到满」的意思。

items.example: The noun names the missing piece.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名缺失的那一块。

items.example: English keeps both the thing and the act.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留物与动作。

items.example: The adjective describes the relation between two parts.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述两部分之间的关系。

items.example: The noun belongs to grammar and biology.
items.exampleCN: 名词用于语法与生物学。

items.example: The same filling verb gives the everyday word.
items.exampleCN: 同一「填满」动词给出日常词。

items.meaning: an addition to improve or extend
items.example: The word adds rather than completes.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是添加，而非补全。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the filling thing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把动词变成填充之物。

definition_zh: adj. 互补的；补充的
definition_en: combining well so that each supplies what the other lacks
core_image: 钥匙与锁孔刚好对上，缺一不可
scene: 这两种药作用互补，医生常一起开。The two drugs are complementary, so doctors often prescribe both.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：complementary 指互补的；句意是这两种药作用互补，医生常一起开。

senses.title: Filling what the other lacks
senses.definition: combining with something so that the pair works better
senses.definitionCN: 与另一物合起来效果更好
senses.example: Their skills are complementary.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的技能互补。
senses.why: Latin complere means to fill up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 complere 意为填满。

senses.title: Used alongside standard treatment
senses.definition: used in addition to, not instead of, the main method
senses.definitionCN: 作为主要方法之外的附加手段
senses.example: She studies complementary medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究补充医学。
senses.why: Medicine gave the word this narrower sense.
senses.whyCN: 医学界赋予它这一较窄的义项。

intro.en: Complementary comes from a Latin verb meaning to fill up.
intro.cn: complementary 源自拉丁语「填满」的动词。

items.en: Plere means to fill.
items.cn: plere 意为填满。

items.en: Complere means to fill up completely.
items.cn: complere 意为完全填满。

items.en: It names what completes a thing.
items.cn: 该词指使事物完整者。

items.en: Complementary describes things that complete each other.
items.cn: 十七世纪 complementary 形容互相补足之物。

items.en: Colour theory fixed the sense of paired hues.
items.cn: 十九世纪色彩理论固定了配对色之义。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts the two spellings; the near-meaning group names pairing.
note.cn: 形近组对比两种拼写；近义组列出配对关系。

normalIntro.en: Complementary things fill each other out.
normalIntro.cn: complementary 之物互相补足。

normal.en: Plere means to fill.
normal.cn: plere 意为填满。

normal.en: Complere means to fill up.
normal.cn: complere 意为填满。

normal.en: Complement is what completes.
normal.cn: complement 是补全之物。

normal.en: Complementary means completing each other.
normal.cn: complementary 意为互相补全。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with complimentary.
normal.cn: 别与 complimentary（赞美的）混淆。

abstract.en: A key and its lock.
abstract.cn: 钥匙与锁。

abstract.en: Two dancers balanced.
abstract.cn: 相互平衡的两名舞者。

abstract.en: Blue beside orange.
abstract.cn: 橙色旁的蓝色。

examples.en: The two approaches are complementary.
examples.cn: 这两种方法互补。

examples.en: They have complementary strengths.
examples.cn: 他们的长处互补。

examples.en: The clinic offers complementary therapy.
examples.cn: 这家诊所提供补充疗法。

dict_mnemonic.text: complement（补足）+ -ary（…的）→ 能互相补足的，即互补的。

root: 拉丁 com（完全）+ plere（填满）→ complementum → complement → complementary

sensesIntro.en: A pair that completes each other, and a treatment added beside another.
sensesIntro.cn: 彼此补全的一对，以及附加于另一种疗法之旁的疗法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key turning perfectly in its lock
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙在锁孔里恰好转动

branches.en: Blue and orange side by side.
branches.cn: 并排的蓝与橙。

branches.en: One plans, the other builds.
branches.cn: 一个规划，一个施工。

branches.en: Massage offered beside surgery.
branches.cn: 手术之外提供的按摩。

branches.en: A clinic with two kinds of care.
branches.cn: 提供两类护理的诊所。

branches.en: What is added to make a whole.
branches.cn: 为成全整体而增添之物。

intro.en: Complementary is built from filling pieces; the list adds completion words.
intro.cn: complementary 由「填满」词素构成；下面列出补全词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin plere is to fill, complere is to fill up, and complementum is a completion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plere 意为填满，complere 意为填满，complementum 意为补全。

latinEntries.exampleCN: complere 产生 complete 与 complement。
plere 促成 complete 与 supply。

definition_zh: 完成；完整的；彻底的
definition_en: to finish making something whole, or having every part and nothing missing
core_image: 最后一块拼图落位，整幅画终于没有缺口
scene: 木匠把最后一块板钉上，柜子刚好合缝。It took him a month to complete the cabinet.
sceneCN: 这里 complete 指「完成」（第 1 个义项：做完某事）；句意是他花了一个月才把柜子做完。

senses.title: To finish
senses.definition: to finish doing or making something
senses.definitionCN: 做完或制成某物
senses.example: She completed the report before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她中午前完成了报告。
senses.why: The verb looks at the last step that closes a gap.
senses.whyCN: 动词着眼于补上缺口的那最后一步。

senses.title: Whole, with nothing missing
senses.definition: having every part and no gaps
senses.definitionCN: 各部分齐全、没有缺漏
senses.example: The museum owns a complete set of these coins.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆藏有这套钱币的完整一套。
senses.why: The adjective describes the state the last step leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述最后一步留下的状态。

senses.title: Total and thorough
senses.definition: used to stress that something is total
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事是彻底的
senses.example: The plan was a complete failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划彻底失败了。
senses.why: If nothing is missing, the whole thing can also be called complete in degree.
senses.whyCN: 若一无所缺，整体在程度上也可称作彻底。

intro.en: Complete comes from Latin complere, to fill up, from com, completely, and plere, to fill.
intro.cn: complete 来自拉丁语 complere，意为填满，由 com（完全）与 plere（填充）构成。

items.en: Plere meant to fill something up.
items.cn: plere 意为把某物填满。

items.en: Complere meant to fill until nothing was missing.
items.cn: complere 意为填到一点不缺。

items.en: Completus described a thing fully filled.
items.cn: completus 描述被完全填满的事物。

items.en: Old French complet kept the sense of whole.
items.cn: 古法语 complet 保留了「完整」的意思。

items.en: English complete grew both a verb and an adjective use.
items.cn: 英语 complete 长出动词与形容词两种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words one letter from complete, and the meaning group separates finishing, wholeness and total degree.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 complete 只差一个字母的词，近义组分辨做完、完整与彻底程度。

entries.definition: to bring something to an end

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with the last puzzle piece, then move to the whole it leaves and to the total degree it can name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从最后一块拼图开始，再走到它留下的整体以及它能表示的彻底程度。

normal.en: Com- means fully and plere means fill, so complete is filled to the top.
normal.cn: com- 表示完全，plere 表示填满，complete 就是填到顶。

normal.en: As a verb, complete means to close the last gap.
normal.cn: 作动词时，complete 意为补上最后的缺口。

normal.en: As an adjective, complete means no part is missing.
normal.cn: 作形容词时，complete 意为没有一部分缺失。

normal.en: A complete failure is not a finished one, but a total one.
normal.cn: a complete failure 不是「完成了的失败」，而是「彻底的失败」。

normal.en: The noun is completion, and the opposite adjective is incomplete.
normal.cn: 名词是 completion，反面形容词是 incomplete。

abstract.en: Picture a puzzle with only one empty space left.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅拼图只剩一个小空格。

abstract.en: Picture a full set of keys on one ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一整串钥匙挂在一个环上。

abstract.en: Picture a room so quiet that the clock is loud.
abstract.cn: 想象房间静得连钟声都显得响。

examples.en: Please complete the form in black ink.
examples.cn: 请用黑色墨水填完这张表。

examples.en: The collection is now complete.
examples.cn: 这套收藏现在完整了。

examples.en: His answer was complete nonsense.
examples.cn: 他的回答完全是胡扯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 complete 记成 com（一起）加 plete（填满）：把空缺全填满，就是完成与完整。

root: 源自拉丁语 complere，com- 表示全部，plere 表示填满，本义是填满、使无空缺，后引申为完成、完整的与彻底的。

sensesIntro.en: From the last step that fills a gap, to the whole that results, and finally to total degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 从填上缺口的最后一步，到由此得到的整体，最后到彻底的程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last piece clicks in and the picture has no empty space.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一块拼图落位，整幅画终于没有缺口。

branches.en: The verb names the act of closing the gap.
branches.cn: 动词指补上缺口的那个动作。

branches.en: The adjective names the whole that no longer has a gap.
branches.cn: 形容词指不再有缺口的整体。

branches.en: If nothing is missing, the degree can also be called complete.
branches.cn: 若一无所缺，程度也可以叫彻底。

branches.en: The act and the state are two sides of one filling.
branches.cn: 动作与状态是同一次填充的两面。

branches.en: A whole thing can also be wholly one way.
branches.cn: 一个完整的东西，也可以在程度上完全是某种样子。

intro.en: Complete is built on Latin com, fully, plus plere, to fill.
intro.cn: complete 由拉丁语 com（完全）加 plere（填充）构成。

latinIntro.en: The filling base plere also appears in supply and in supplement.
latinIntro.cn: 表示填充的词基 plere 也出现在 supply 与 supplement 里。

items.example: She completes each task on time.
items.exampleCN: 她按时完成每一项任务。

items.example: The bridge was completed in May.
Completing the form takes five minutes.
The editor checks the completeness of the file.
items.exampleCN: 编辑检查文件是否完整。

definition_zh: 复杂的；综合体；情结
definition_en: made of many connected parts that are hard to understand, or a group of buildings, or a strong feeling fixed in the mind
core_image: 一团缠在一起的线，越拉越紧
scene: 新小区里有住宅、商铺和一所小学，走进去容易迷路。The new complex includes homes, shops and a school.
sceneCN: 这里 complex 指「综合体」（第 2 个义项：由多部分组成的建筑群）；句意是这个新综合体包含住宅、商铺和一所小学。

senses.title: Hard to understand
senses.definition: having many parts that are connected in ways hard to follow
senses.definitionCN: 由许多部分以难以理清的方式相连
senses.example: The tax rules are far too complex for most people.
senses.exampleCN: 税法对大多数人来说太复杂了。
senses.why: Many parts plus many links is exactly what makes a thing hard to hold in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 部分多、牵连多，正是事物难以在脑中把握的原因。

senses.title: A group of buildings
senses.definition: a group of buildings or facilities used for one purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为同一用途建起的一组建筑或设施
senses.example: The sports complex has two pools and a gym.
senses.exampleCN: 这个体育中心有两个泳池和一间健身房。
senses.why: Parts gathered on one site become a whole that carries one name.
senses.whyCN: 聚集在同一场地上的部分，成了一个共用一个名字的整体。

senses.title: A fixed feeling
senses.definition: a strong feeling or idea that is fixed in a person's mind
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢盘踞在人心里的强烈感受或念头
senses.example: He still has a complex about his accent.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己的口音仍有心结。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word for feelings woven so tightly that they hold the mind.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借这个词，指缠绕得紧紧、抓住人心的感受。

intro.en: Complex comes from Latin complecti, to embrace or intertwine, whose participle is complexus.
intro.cn: complex 来自拉丁语 complecti，意为拥抱或交织，其分词形式是 complexus。

items.en: Plectere meant to weave or to twine.
items.cn: plectere 意为编织或缠绕。

items.en: Complecti meant to wrap around and hold together.
items.cn: complecti 意为缠绕包围、抱在一起。

items.en: Complexus described things woven into one.
items.cn: complexus 描述被织成一体的东西。

items.en: English complex first meant made of connected parts.
items.cn: 英语 complex 最初指由相互连接的部分组成。

items.en: It expanded to building groups and to fixed feelings.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到建筑群以及盘踞不去的感受。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close to complex in sound, and the meaning group ranks complicated, intricate and a network of parts.
note.cn: 形近组收的是读音与 complex 相近的词，近义组排出复杂难懂、错综复杂与相互连接的部分。

entries.definition: the natural colour of the skin
hard to understand because of many parts
having many small parts arranged finely

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with tangled thread, then move to many buildings on one site and to a knot held in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从缠住的线开始，再走到同一场地上的一片建筑以及心里的一个结。

normal.en: Com- is together and plex means weave, so complex is woven together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，plex 是编织，complex 就是被织在一起。

normal.en: Many parts plus many links equals complex.
normal.cn: 部分多、连接多，就等于复杂。

normal.en: A sports complex is one site holding many facilities.
normal.cn: 体育综合体就是一块场地上装着许多设施。

normal.en: An inferiority complex is a knot that keeps pulling tight.
normal.cn: 自卑情结就是一个越拉越紧的结。

normal.en: Complex is the thing; complexity is the quality it has.
normal.cn: complex 是那个东西，complexity 是它具备的性质。

abstract.en: Picture a ball of thread where one pull tightens everything.
abstract.cn: 想象一团线，一拉反而更紧。

abstract.en: Picture one gate opening onto homes, shops and a school.

examples.cn: 人脑是一个极其复杂的器官。

root: 源自拉丁语 complecti（缠绕、拥抱）与 complexus，本义是交织在一起的，后引申为复杂的、综合体与情结。

sensesIntro.en: From many tangled parts, to many buildings on one site, and finally to a knot in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 从交织的许多部分，到同一场地上的一片建筑，最后到心里的一个结。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball of thread tangled so tightly that pulling makes it worse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团缠在一起的线，越拉越紧。

branches.en: Many parts and many links make the first sense.
branches.cn: 部分多、连接多，造出了第一个义项。

branches.en: Buildings gathered on one site carry the same name.
branches.cn: 聚在同一场地的建筑沿用同一个名字。

branches.en: A feeling woven that tightly becomes a complex.
branches.cn: 一种感受缠得那么紧，就成了情结。

branches.en: Both senses gather parts into one whole.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把部分聚成一个整体。

branches.en: A tangle in the world and a tangle in the mind share one image.
branches.cn: 世上的乱麻与心里的乱麻共用一个意象。

intro.en: Complex is built on Latin com, together, plus plectere, to weave.
intro.cn: complex 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 plectere（编织）构成。

latinIntro.en: The weaving base also appears in perplex, to weave someone into confusion.
latinIntro.cn: 表示编织的词基也出现在 perplex 里，意为把人织进困惑。

items.example: The complexity of the rules surprised us.

items.example: She explained the complexities of the case.
